basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/Datazag/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [Datazag](https://datazag.com/) solution for Microsoft Sentinel delivers impersonation and attacker-infrastructure indicators derived from Certificate Transparency at issuance time, published as STIX 2.1 objects over a TAXII 2.1 server. Indicators are ingested using Microsoft Sentinel's built-in **Threat Intelligence - TAXII** data connector and land in the native **ThreatIntelIndicators** table. No custom table, data collection rule or workspace function is required, and indicators are available to analytics rules and hunting queries immediately. Because indicators are retained in the workspace, existing logs can also be retro-hunted against them. **Prerequisites:** a. An active Datazag subscription. Contact Datazag to obtain the API root, collection ID and credentials. b. Analytic rules and hunting queries in this solution query DNS activity through the [Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/normalization). The relevant ASIM parsers must be deployed in the workspace for this content to return results. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 1, **Hunting Queries:** 1 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: Datazag - impersonation domain resolved in DNS

options.text:
Matches active Datazag domain indicators against DNS query activity normalized by the ASIM
Dns schema. Reading from the ASIM parser rather than a vendor-specific table means the rule
works across any normalized DNS source in the workspace (Windows DNS, Infoblox, Cisco
Umbrella, Azure Firewall, Zscaler and others) without modification. The ASIM DNS parsers
must be deployed in the workspace for this rule to return results.

A match means a host inside the estate resolved a domain that Datazag scored as brand
impersonation, platform impersonation or attacker infrastructure at or above the configured
confidence floor. Resolution is not proof of compromise, but it establishes that the domain
reached a resolver from inside the estate, which is the earliest observable point in most
credential-phishing chains.

Indicators are identified by their STIX created_by_ref rather than by SourceSystem, because
SourceSystem reflects the friendly name chosen when the TAXII connector was configured and
therefore differs between deployments.

Indicator revisions are collapsed with arg_max by Id, so a re-derived indicator does not
produce duplicate matches. Withdrawn, revoked and expired indicators are excluded.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: Datazag - retro-hunt historical DNS against impersonation indicators

options.text:
Sweeps the workspace DNS history against the current Datazag indicator set to answer the
question "what did we already miss?".

This is the query to run immediately after connecting the Datazag TAXII feed. Indicators are
retained in the workspace, so they can be matched against logs that predate the connection.
A domain detected by Datazag at certificate issuance may have been resolved inside the estate
weeks before the feed was configured.

The lookback is deliberately wider than any scheduled analytic rule can use, which is why
this is a hunting query rather than a rule. Adjust dns_lookback to match your DNS retention.

If DNS logs are held in an auxiliary or data lake tier rather than the analytics tier, they
are not reachable from advanced hunting and must be queried through the data lake
exploration experience instead. This hunting query depends on DatazagThreatIntelligence data connector (ThreatIntelIndicators Parser or Table)
